checks: The positive support is the effective domain of the convex inverse power. The interior ball gives finite continuous g and an upper bound A there.
The contracted ball has volume a^r times the original volume; using a=ε/A gives the stated ε^(r−β) estimate. For g(x)=0 the same contraction with arbitrary a forces infinite mass since β>r.

An unbounded sublevel containing a central ball would contain cones of unbounded volume; the same argument in dimension one uses intervals. Testing the segment at radius R gives g(x)>g(0)(1+||x||/R), and the bounded-radius lower bound handles all remaining points.

Integrating the pointwise lower and upper estimates yields positive finite radial integrals uniformly in directions, including β=r+1. Checked 1c081cc96e28cc4a §1 and formula (2) against the exact normalized scope.

overlap.comparison: The accepted strict-exponent radial theorem proves interior positivity and bounded radial extent for β>r+1. It does not supply the global pointwise envelope, exclusion of infinite values everywhere, or the critical exponent.

readability: The exponent argument uses β>r; the staged statement keeps the source's β≥r+1 range.
review_method: Independent cold mathematical proof review with exact symbolic and rational replays where applicable.
summary: The mass bound forces positive inverse power everywhere it is finite. A bounded convex sublevel then gives the stated global decay and uniform radial bounds at every interior anchor.
